body:
Proposed. The dot is the community separator: zmx's own example is `d.term` for `Host d.*`, zp creates `<repo>.<n>`, and zmx's prefix matchers are written `zmx kill 'd.*'`. Aligning means `zmx kill 'zmux.*'`, `zmx wait 'test*'` and zp's repo sessions all agree, and a dot is already inside the label-safe set [a-zA-Z0-9-_.].

Rules: the first dot separates project from id; dots inside either component fold to `-` during sanitisation, so the split stays unambiguous in the one place it matters (a human reading it); `<>` and spaces fold to `-`.

Caveat this does not fix: d-naming still holds — the name is convenience and the labels are truth, because wildcard matching is prefix-based and a project name containing a dot can still shadow another prefix.
title: Name sessions <project>.<id>, not <project>-<id>
